status_summary: The 2025 reconciliation law (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) provides about $7.5 billion in Sec. 20001 for military quality of life, including an expansion of privatized military housing construction, per CRS. The FY2026 NDAA (Public Law 119-60, signed 2025-12-18) contains sections modifying the enlisted basic allowance for subsistence, increasing the family separation allowance (to $300 a month per Military Times), improving the basic allowance for housing and reviewing child care fee assistance limits, and a House member's release reports a 3.8 percent pay raise and extension of the in-home child care pilot through 2029. A Department of War memo of 2026-04-01 told components to make maximum use of spouse employment flexibilities, and Executive Order 14417 (signed 2026-08-03) created a President's Military Spouse Commission to develop policies on housing, employment and other spouse concerns. No raise targeted at junior enlisted pay was enacted for 2026, and licensing reform appears in the order only as background.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was enacted; its Sec. 20001 provides about $7.5 billion for military quality of life, including expanded privatized military housing construction (per CRS).

The President signed the FY2026 NDAA (S. 1071, Public Law 119-60), whose table of contents lists Sec. 621 (enlisted basic allowance for subsistence), Sec. 622 (family separation allowance increase), Sec. 624 (basic allowance for housing improvements) and Sec. 641 (child care fee assistance review).

The Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness issued a memo directing fuller use of military spouse employment flexibilities, including a pilot letting spouses accept federal jobs before arriving at a new duty station.
Executive Order 14417 established the President's Military Spouse Commission to develop policies on housing, employment, health care, education and deployment support for military spouses.

title: Raise enlisted pay and allowances, improve housing, spouse jobs and childcare
uncertainties: Section text of Public Law 119-60 is not in the GovInfo HTML copy (the page holds only the table of contents and front matter), so section contents rest on section titles, a House member's release, Military Times and MOAA; the exact BAS mechanics and the BAH terms were not read. The 3.8 percent raise is the formula-based raise for all members; whether it counts as increasing wages in the Mandate's sense is a judgment call. A Marine Corps message reproduced on an unofficial mirror says the $300 family separation allowance applies retroactively to 2025-12-18; it was not used as a source. The FY2025 NDAA (Public Law 118-159) targeted junior enlisted raises predate the period. CRS does not break out child care or spouse items within Sec. 20001 of Public Law 119-21. The April 2026 memo was read only through MOAA. Spouse licensing and childcare capacity expansion were not found as new actions. The FY2027 request (7 percent for E-1 to E-5 per CRS) is not enacted.
